signatures.name: [Redfisher] Redfish API over unencrypted HTTP
signatures.description: Redfish API traffic was observed over plain HTTP. Authentication tokens and credentials are transmitted in cleartext.
signatures.background: The Redfish specification requires HTTPS for all API communication. HTTP exposes X-Auth-Token headers and Basic auth credentials to network-level attackers.
signatures.remediation: Configure the BMC to only accept HTTPS. Disable HTTP on the management interface.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Session token exposed in response body
signatures.description: The response body contains a literal X-Auth-Token key. Tokens should only appear in response headers, not in the JSON body.
signatures.background: Redfish session tokens returned in JSON bodies may be logged by proxies and application layers that capture response bodies but not headers.
signatures.remediation: Return session tokens only via the X-Auth-Token response header.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Sensitive fields exposed in Redfish response
signatures.description: The response contains sensitive field(s) with non-null values. These fields should be omitted or masked in GET responses.
signatures.background: Redfish compliant implementations must not return plaintext passwords, private keys, or authentication credentials in GET responses.
signatures.remediation: Return null for sensitive fields in read responses. Only accept them as write-only inputs.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Missing security headers on Redfish response
signatures.description: The Redfish response is missing one or more security headers.
signatures.background: Security headers prevent browser-based attacks such as MIME-type sniffing and clickjacking.
signatures.remediation: Add the missing security headers to all Redfish API responses.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Session token in URL
signatures.description: A potential session token was detected in the URL query string. Tokens in URLs are stored in browser history, server logs, and proxy access logs.
signatures.background: Tokens must be transmitted in headers, never in URLs.
signatures.remediation: Pass the X-Auth-Token in the request header, not in the URL.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Credentials transmitted over HTTP
signatures.description: A Redfish session creation request contains a Password field and is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP.
signatures.background: Credentials POSTed to the session endpoint over HTTP are exposed to any network observer.
signatures.remediation: Enforce HTTPS on the Redfish management interface.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] OData debug information exposed
signatures.description: The response contains OData debug or error detail information that may expose internal system paths or stack traces.
signatures.background: Verbose OData error messages can reveal internal implementation details useful to an attacker.
signatures.remediation: Configure the Redfish service to return minimal error detail in production.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Redfish version information disclosed
signatures.description: The server response header exposes the software version of the management firmware.
signatures.background: Version disclosure allows attackers to target known vulnerabilities for the specific firmware version.
signatures.remediation: Suppress or genericise the Server response header.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Unauthenticated access to Redfish endpoint
signatures.description: The Redfish endpoint returned a success response when accessed without any authentication headers. Expected 401 or 403.
signatures.background: All Redfish endpoints except the Service Root require authentication. Access without credentials should always return 401 Unauthorized.
signatures.remediation: Configure the BMC to require authentication on all Redfish endpoints. Verify session handling rules are applied globally.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Default credentials accepted
signatures.description: The Redfish session endpoint accepted a well-known default credential pair.
signatures.background: Default factory credentials are a well-known attack vector for BMC/management controllers. Attackers routinely scan for these credentials on internal networks.
signatures.remediation: Change all default credentials immediately after deployment. Enforce a strong password policy and disable default accounts where possible.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Auth token in URL query string
signatures.description: An authentication token was found in the URL query string. Tokens in URLs are logged by web servers, proxies, and browser history.
signatures.background: Redfish tokens should only be transmitted in the X-Auth-Token request header, never in URLs.
signatures.remediation: Remove token from URL and transmit only via X-Auth-Token header.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] BIOS attributes with sensitive data exposed
signatures.description: BIOS attributes endpoint returned fields with names suggesting password, key, or credential data with non-null values.
signatures.background: Some BMC implementations return BIOS passwords or NVMe keys in /Bios/Attributes responses. This constitutes plaintext credential exposure.
signatures.remediation: Ensure sensitive BIOS attributes are masked or omitted from GET responses. Apply role-based access restrictions to Bios endpoints.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Firmware HTTP upload URI exposed
signatures.description: The UpdateService response contains an HttpPushUri field, exposing a firmware upload endpoint.
signatures.background: If firmware upload does not require signed images or enforce role-based access, an attacker with credentials can flash malicious firmware.
signatures.remediation: Ensure firmware upload requires Administrator role, validates digital signatures, and logs all attempts.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] BMC version disclosed in Server header
signatures.description: The Server response header reveals the BMC vendor and/or firmware version, aiding targeted attacks.
signatures.background: Banner information helps attackers select version-specific exploits and known CVEs without needing additional reconnaissance.
signatures.remediation: Configure the BMC to suppress or genericise the Server header.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Privilege escalation via PATCH account role
signatures.description: A PATCH request to an account URL successfully changed the RoleId to Administrator, indicating missing authorisation enforcement.
signatures.background: Redfish AccountService must restrict role modification to Administrator-privileged sessions. If unprivileged users can escalate their role, full BMC compromise follows.
signatures.remediation: Enforce role-based access control on PATCH /AccountService/Accounts/{id}. Return 403 for non-admin role change attempts.

signatures.name: [Redfisher] Unauthenticated session creation
signatures.description: A session token was issued in response to a POST request that contained no authentication headers.
signatures.background: The SessionService/Sessions endpoint must validate credentials before issuing tokens. Unauthenticated session creation bypasses all BMC access controls.
signatures.remediation: Require valid UserName/Password credentials and return 401 for missing or invalid credentials.
